name: Battle of Marengo
note: The accounts give the places of the villages only as a triangle (Marengo west, Castel Ceriolo north, San Giuliano Vecchio east), so distances here are schematic. The accounts do not say where Kellermann's cavalry stood before its last charge; it is placed on the northern side of the Austrian column. Frimont's cavalry, which destroyed the Guard, is drawn with the Austrian left wing, with which the accounts have him act.

phases.title: The two armies take their ground
phases.text: The Austrians crossed the Bormida in three bodies. Victor held Marengo and the Fontanone with Kellermann's cavalry on his left, Lannes stood to the north-east, and Monnier and the Guard waited east of Castel Ceriolo.
phases.quote: The movement began about 6 am with the first shots fired around 8 am, but the attack was not fully developed until 9 am.

phases.title: The Austrian assaults at the Fontanone fail
phases.text: Melas sent his divisions at Marengo across the stream one after another. Forced into a funnel by the ground, the first attack failed under fire from two sides, and the second was beaten off by 11 am.
phases.quote: Forced into a funnel by the bad ground and Fontanone stream, Hadik's attack came under fire from two sides and failed, with Hadik being killed.

phases.title: Ott takes Castel Ceriolo and presses the French right
phases.text: Ott's leading troops took Castel Ceriolo and began to press the French right flank. Monnier's division and the Guard were brought across to extend and shore up that flank.
phases.quote: but soon Ott's lead units took it around 11:30 am and began putting pressure on the French right flank

phases.title: Victor withdraws from Marengo
phases.text: The Austrians bridged the Fontanone and took Marengo. Victor could no longer hold his positions and fell back south-east to the vine belt, with Lannes mirroring the move, while O'Reilly took Stortiglione.
phases.quote: However, Victor could no longer hold his positions and withdrew southeast to the main vine belt

phases.title: The French fall back and the Guard is destroyed
phases.text: Ott defeated Monnier, and two thirds of his division retreated north-east. The Guard, sent to delay Schellenberg's column, was surprised and destroyed. The French fell back about 3 km towards San Giuliano as the Austrian centre formed a pursuit column.
phases.quote: The French fell back c. 3 km and attempted to regroup to hold the village of San Giuliano.

phases.title: Desaix's force arrives and meets the column
phases.text: Boudet's division was deployed in front of San Giuliano and advanced in line of brigades against the head of the Austrian column, defeating its leading brigade. The column came on along the road.
phases.quote: Boudet's division advanced in line of brigades against the head of the Austrian column, defeating Saint-Julien's leading Austrian brigade.

phases.title: Kellermann's charge breaks the Austrian centre
phases.text: Kellermann's heavy cavalry charged the left flank of the Austrian grenadier brigade, which disintegrated. The Austrian centre lost heart and rushed to the rear while the French infantry line advanced westward.
phases.quote: Lattermann's formation was charged on its left flank by Kellermann's heavy cavalry (ca. 400 men) and disintegrated.
